1:
I followed the instruction to keep the financing report as one evidence item because the article presents it as one deal, with its amount, proposed financing structure, participants, and uncertainty:

> “the same fact said again in other words within this item: one deal, hire, programme or reported measure told in several sentences, with its terms, figures and growth rates, is one evidence item; keep the fuller wording”

I also applied the instruction to quote the evidence verbatim:

> “Copy its quote verbatim, without translation.”

And the instruction that each item should capture the source statement and its relevant context:

> “One evidence item records one statement, and that statement is what you judge”

I weighed those against the requirement to walk through the article and identify each research matter:

> “Walk the article from beginning to end. Identify each research matter and what the source actually says”

I should have kept the quote to the contiguous passage supporting the financing report. The after-hours share-price sentence is a separate statement, and it is excluded by the instruction:

> “a share-price move or an investor's position or trade (‘shares fell 13% this month’; ‘he is short the stock’)”

So joining separate paragraphs into one non-contiguous quote was not justified by the one-evidence-item rule; that rule says to consolidate repeated wording about the same fact, not to present separated text as a verbatim passage.
2:
No instruction led me to join those paragraphs. That was an error: the instructions say to “Copy its quote verbatim,” and “One evidence item records one statement.” The quoted financing and the sentence about after-hours trading are separate statements, so I should not have assembled a quote across the intervening text or omitted that sentence while presenting the assembled text as a verbatim passage.

I should also have weighed the instruction to “Walk the article from beginning to end” and identify “each research matter and what the source actually says,” alongside the instruction to keep a statement only when it passes the closing check. The financing report may be relevant to Nvidia revenue, but that does not justify altering the article’s wording or combining separate passages.
